requirement_text.REQ-425:
MOB-6 in docs/mobile/requirements.md (build-order M6; depends on M2). Built BEFORE MOB-4 (REQ-426..428) -- see the S9 header: the renderers' six states classify this requirement's ApiError. SECURITY-REVIEWER gate (refresh-token handling, token clearing).

Hardens lib/api/api_client.dart (created by REQ-421) into the single client:
1. Attach the active tenant's bearer token (REQ-422's iss check).
2. On 401: exactly one silent refresh via flutter_appauth's token refresh, then exactly one retry of the original request; concurrent 401s share one in-flight refresh. On refresh failure: clear the tenant's tokens (REQ-422 store) and route to login.
3. Exponential backoff on 5xx for idempotent methods only (GET), bounded attempts; POST is not auto-retried (no duplicate task completion).
4. Normalise every failure to a sealed ApiError type before it leaves lib/api/: at minimum network-unavailable, unauthorized, forbidden (403), not-found, module-not-available (a 404 on any /api/v1/modules/<id>/ path -- architecture.md §6: absence is 404, not 403, and must not render as a generic not-found), backpressure (429, carrying the Retry-After seconds -- the backend emits 429 from lib/letflow/plugs/admission.ex and lib/letflow/plugs/public_read_rate_limit.ex), validation (422 with RFC 9457 field errors), conflict (409), server (5xx after retries).
5. A static guard (apps/mobile/test/guards/), the counterpart of the SPA's raw-fetch-outside-client guard in web/tests/guards/: no file outside lib/api/ imports package:dio or package:http or uses dart:io HttpClient; with a self-test.

task.description: Step 1b of WF-02 for REQ-425. Read lib/letflow/design/req425-mobile-api-client-hardening.md directly (not CODE-DESIGNER's handoff result.summary as a substitute). For each of the 7 acceptance criteria below, verify: (a) it has a corresponding design element, no TBD/deferral language; (b) function signatures are fully specified (name, inputs, outputs, error cases); (c) error handling shape is stated as tagged/sealed types, not left implicit; (d) cross-module dependencies are listed; (e) no implementation code is present -- signatures and type shapes only, no .dart function bodies. Pay particular attention to: the module-vs-plain-404 path-matching rule (must be an exact, testable rule, not vague prose), the terminal behavior when a SECOND 401 occurs on the already-retried request (must not describe an infinite loop, and must state the explicit terminal rule), the 5xx backoff formula (must be exact and deterministic/fake-clock-testable, with a named bounded-attempts constant), and the guard's self-test fixture design (must specify exactly what triggers a flag vs. not). FAIL immediately on any check failure -- no partial credit. Claim by setting status to IN_PROGRESS.
acceptance_criteria: a test where the fake server returns 401 once then 200 asserts exactly one refresh call and exactly one retry, and that two concurrent requests both receiving 401 trigger one refresh total
a test where refresh fails asserts the tenant's tokens are deleted from the secure store and the router is at the login route

a test asserts a GET receiving 503 twice then 200 succeeds with increasing delays between attempts (fake clock), a GET receiving 503 on every attempt stops after the maximum attempt count declared as a named constant in lib/api/ and surfaces ApiError server (the test asserts the exact number of requests sent), and a POST receiving 503 is not retried

a test per ApiError variant asserts the mapping from status code/exception, including 404 on /api/v1/modules/exam/x -> module-not-available, 404 elsewhere -> not-found, and 429 with 'Retry-After: 7' -> backpressure(7 seconds)
a test asserts no DioException or SocketException escapes lib/api/ -- the public client API returns or throws only ApiError
the single-client guard fails its self-test fixture (a file under lib/features/ importing package:dio) and passes on the real tree
cd apps/mobile && flutter analyze && flutter test pass, real output quoted, and SECURITY-REVIEWER signs off before merge

result.summary: FAIL. Read lib/letflow/design/req425-mobile-api-client-hardening.md directly (853 lines) and independently re-derived all 7 acceptance criteria against it. ACs 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 each have a fully-specified corresponding design element (exact refresh-coordinator Future-caching shape and concurrency behavior for AC1 -- Sec 2.1-2.3; exact token-delete + login-routing sequence for AC2 -- Sec 2.2 step 5; exact named retry-count constant kMaxServerRetryAttempts=3, deterministic exponential backoff formula with injectable delayFn, and POST-not-retried rule for AC3 -- Sec 3.1-3.3; exact status/exception-to-ApiError mapping table including the module-path regex ^/api/v1/modules/([^/]+)/ with worked examples and Retry-After parsing for AC4 -- Sec 1.2-1.4; explicit throw-ApiError-only convention for AC5 -- Sec 5.1; exact guard scan rules and fixture behavior for AC6 -- Sec 4.1-4.3). The task's four flagged focus areas (module-vs-plain-404 rule, second-401 terminal behavior, 5xx backoff formula, guard self-test fixture) are each exact and testable, not vague prose -- in isolation these would have passed. However two independent hard-gate violations were found that require FAIL with no partial credit: (1) TBD/deferral language present on a function central to AC1's refresh mechanism -- Sec 5.2's AppAuthAdapter.refresh doc comment states '...or its token-refresh-response equivalent -- see OQ-2, exact flutter_appauth type/method TBD...', i.e. the literal word 'TBD' appears describing the exact API shape of the one genuinely-new call this whole requirement introduces (no refresh call exists anywhere in the tree today per the design's own Sec 0). This is not a peripheral open question; it is the mechanism AC1 and AC2 are built on, left admittedly unverified against the actual pinned flutter_appauth ^12.1.0 API. (2) Real implementation code present, not signatures/type-shapes only -- Sec 4.2 contains a full Dart test function body with executable logic (constructs a fixture map, calls checkSingleApiClientBoundary, and asserts via expect(violations, hasLength(1)) and expect(violations.single.file, ...)), violating the design doc's own stated rule (its own preamble: 'No implementation code appears below -- @spec-style signatures, type/field shapes... only') and this gate's check (e). A minor additional defect noted for the record (not independently gate-failing but compounds the ambiguity risk cited as this gate's exact purpose): Sec 5.1's ApiClient class snippet declares 'Future<Response<dynamic>> post(String path, {Object? data});' twice (lines ~659 and ~669) with different doc comments, an unresolved copy-paste inconsistency a real implementer would have to guess how to resolve. Routing back to CODE-DESIGNER: (a) replace the TBD language in Sec 5.2 by actually reading flutter_appauth ^12.1.0's real API (pubspec.lock / package source) and stating the exact method/type the refresh call uses, or if genuinely infeasible to verify at design time, restate AppAuthAdapter.refresh's contract without the word TBD and escalate the verification need to REVIEWER/MOBILE-DEV explicitly as a routing note rather than leaving unverified language inside the function's own doc comment; (b) remove or rewrite Sec 4.2's test bodies as prose/spec description of exactly what fixture input produces what violation-count output, without executable Dart code; (c) resolve or remove the duplicate 'post' declaration in Sec 5.1.
issues: TBD language on AppAuthAdapter.refresh (Sec 5.2) -- the exact API shape of the core new refresh mechanism (AC1/AC2) is left unverified with the literal word 'TBD', not just an open question about a peripheral detail

Sec 4.2 contains full executable Dart test function bodies (fixture construction + expect() assertions), not signatures/type-shapes -- violates the design's own 'no implementation code' rule and this gate's check (e)
Sec 5.1 declares 'Future<Response<dynamic>> post(String path, {Object? data});' twice with conflicting doc comments -- unresolved duplicate signature

Re-submit to CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR (Step 1b) once revised.
